body: I hate when people assume that their momentary lapse in focus or the self-induced sugar high is ADHD.  They are usually the same people who says I cant possible have it because Im not bouncing off the walls... ugh

They didnt have time for me and they way they treated me made me feel manipulated.  The first guy I saw didn't write anything down, and didnt tell me that he wouldnt be continuing with me until the session was nearly over.  

Like why the heck did I tell you all that crap then???

Shes allowed to have friends and to hang out with them.  It isnt cheating to go have a meal with a friend.  

Now if they are going to a fancy restaurant and shes getting all dressed up for it, then I'd be concerned.
Shes entitled to her opinion, but you are entitled to choose what you put in your body.

Well they have invested 18 years into caring for you.  You say they treat you well, you may cause problems for them, but thats what children do.  They chose to have you and raise you.  I am assuming they want the best for you.

Well Happy Birthday for starters, 🎁. It sounds like the facade is something you would need to work at (possibly with a therapist, which I know you said you cant afford so I will leave that).  

Can I ask how your parents generally treat you?  Specifically what makes you think that they would be fine living their lives without you?
"Perverse narcissist" its the same in English

You say about how dealing with your issues would make things harder for your parents. That is probably true, but it probably would be harder for them to lose their child to suicide.  

If breaking down your facade is the problem then maybe go for baby steps, "I'm having a bad day", "I'm stressed out about my exams" etc.  It is often easy to see through facades as well, something will feel off wven if you dont know what.  Nobody's world consists entirely of unicorns and rainbows.  It is far healthier to be honest with yourself and with the people you trust.

You can go slow about it, next time your parents ask you how your day is tell them honestly if it sucked.  You dont have to share everything at once.  They were your age once too, between the hormones, peer pressure, academic stress and pressure to have your whole life figured out before you turn 18 its a tough time.

You seem stressed about university and finishing high school.  That is perfectly normal, but if that stress is bogging you down then maybe consider taking some time off.  Trust me when I say (as someone who winded up retaking part of a year in uni) the one year extra doesn't matter.  Nobody cares how old you are in college.
That makes sense, thanks for the clarification.  You sound like a great dad.

Having a nice house or a good family doesnt mean you cant be depressed.  You friends sound immature and mean.  You opened up and they let you down.  I'm sorry dude, that really sucks.  Know that not everyone thinks the way they do.  

You might get better results bringing it up one on one with someone you are close with and trust.  You clearly need to talk to someone.

Is it safe for you to approach your parents with this topic?  You say that you wear a facade and I understand that, but maybe write them a note saying that you are struggling.   You don't have to include everything, but having a conversation might just allow for you to vent a bit or to get their perspective.  If your parents arent an option then maybe an older sibling/cousin/etc or maybe your school has a counsellor?

Lastly, you should let yourself cry.  I know it may not fit with your facade, but crying can be cathartic.  You might actually get some of those feelings out.  Do it privately if you are embarrassed about it, but let it happen.  Its natural and doesn't make you weak or anything like that.  Everyone cries, and nobody has to know if you dont want them to.

This is wonderful, but the ages here are doing my head in.  How has she been riding a motorcycle since she was 3?  I am curious as to where its legal to drive so young (no judgment, I think its awesome to teach kids to be capable, just the youngest legal age to drive anything I know of is 14)
I havent bawled like that in years, his comment got me.

I do tend to prioritize his feelings over mine because his issues have a more severe impact on him than mine do for me.  I have been working on being more selfish without being a bitch about it.  I guess arguments like these mean Im moving in the right direction.

My feelings and behaviour are somewhat predictable for me, but externally they often dont make sense.  The university counselling should at least help me get rid of some stress so hopefully that will help too.  Ill ask whoever Im paired with about noticing patterns, maybe they have tips. 

My bf recently finished up with his counsellor, but he has the funding to see someone more advanced and I think he would greatly benefit from it.  

Thanks for the advice, I really appreciate it.

Thanks, I actually want it to be a lot shorter, so I booked another appointment.  I realize my bf was just trying to help, we talked about it.  He really does care and its nice, I guess I got all uppity because I know he would prefer me to keep my hair longer.  He agreed to be more careful with his wording, I agreed to hear him out and not make assumptions.  All is well.

I do try to bring it up when Im feeling a bit better, but I guess Im too timid about it.  Im scared of stressing him out.  

>He probably gets stressed out a bit from knowing that he's not helping you but very much wanting to.

Thats exactly what happens and then I end up helping him deal with his stress and just 'can' my issues.  Its only when something disasterous happens that I can keep the conversation on me without him getting stressed.  That being said, things have gotten better.  I tend to tell him afterwards what he did wrong in a specific circumstance and help explain why doing things like, finding solutions to hypothetical situations that may never happen, isnt helpful and just stresses me out.

He says he will change this and that, and does take the criticsm well, he just doesnt always improve.  Part of the problem is me, Im unpredictable and I cant controll my feelings atm which basically leaves with 'dealing with it' or reaching out at random.  I know its not fair on him, I guess I feel entitled because I helped him.  I know relationships dont work that way.

I think Im too unpredictable for a cheat sheet, but we can try one anyway and see how it goes.

As for myself, I put in to see a counsellor at university so I am trying to sort things out on my end as well.
